lead: A gear fails in one of two places. The root cracks in bending, or the flank pits and wears away. One material must resist both, and the two demands pull against each other: a hard surface needs a soft, tough core underneath. Gear material choice is therefore a system of core strength, surface hardness and heat treatment, matched to load, speed and cost. That choice decides whether a pump gearbox in a Chennai water plant runs ten years or two.
prereq: You need: material properties and factor of safety from Unit 1, and module and pitch diameter from Chapter 7.1.

blocks.text: A tooth is a cantilever. Root bending stress is carried by the whole section, so the core must be strong and tough. A hard, brittle core chips at the root under shock. The flank carries repeated rolling with sliding, and fails by pitting and wear. That is a hardness problem. One material must do both jobs, and still machine well and keep its shape through heat treatment.

Surface hardness is measured as BHN, the Brinell hardness number: a 10 mm steel ball pressed at 3000 kgf, giving hardness in kgf/mm². BHN is not strength in MPa. As a rough estimate for steel, ultimate tensile strength ≈ 3.4 × BHN in MPa, but this comes from a hardness test and is never a design value. The allowable bending stress comes from Chapter 7.3.

The pinion rule matters more than any single number. A 20-tooth pinion driving a 60-tooth gear makes three times the cycles, because it meets every gear tooth once per revolution. Fatigue damage accumulates with cycles, so an equally hard pair wears out first on the pinion. Make the pinion harder by 30–50 BHN. Both wheels then reach the end of life together.

Plain carbon steels with 0.3–0.6% carbon are the shop-floor default. C45 has 0.45% carbon; normalised it is about 220 BHN, and quenched and tempered it reaches 250–300 BHN. It is cheap, machines freely and serves up to about 5 m/s peripheral speed. Above roughly 350 BHN, through-hardening distorts the gear and makes finish machining difficult.

Alloy steels add chromium for hardenability, nickel for core toughness and molybdenum to control tempering and case depth. Through-hardened 40Cr1 or 42CrMo4 reach 300–350 BHN in sections too large for plain carbon steel.

items: Case carburising: a low-carbon steel (0.15–0.25% C with Cr, Ni, Mo) is held at 900–930°C in carbon-rich gas. Carbon diffuses to a depth of 0.8–1.5 mm; the gear is then quenched and tempered. Surface 58–62 HRC, core 30–40 HRC. Chosen for high load and speeds above 5 m/s.

Nitriding: ammonia gas at 500–550°C for many hours, with no quench. Case 0.3–0.5 mm at 500–600 HV. Distortion is very small, so it suits internal gears and large rings that cannot be ground after hardening.
Induction hardening: a coil heats the flanks and they are quenched at once. 50–55 HRC over a tough core, used on large module gears.

blocks.text: Distortion is the hidden cost. A carburised gear must be ground after hardening, so leave 0.1–0.2 mm of stock on each flank and write 'grind after hardening' on the drawing.

Grey cast iron (FG 200, FG 260) contains flake graphite that damps vibration and breaks chips. It machines easily and runs quietly, but its bending strength is low, about 200 MPa. Use it for large, slow gears below about 3–5 m/s, running with a steel pinion. Never use it for a small high-speed pinion.

Bronze belongs to worm wheels, not spur gears. A worm drive slides rather than rolls, so the wheel must be soft, embeddable and low in friction. The standard pair is a phosphor bronze or gunmetal wheel with a hardened, ground steel worm. The bronze is always the softer member.

items: Nylon gears run dry, absorb shock and cost little. They creep, swell with moisture and conduct heat badly, so keep load and speed low.
Bakelite (phenolic laminate) is stiffer and used in timing and cam gears.
Sintered powder-metallurgy gears have 10–15% porosity that holds oil, and are cheap in mass production of small gears.

blocks.text: Selection follows peripheral speed v = πdN/60, where d is pitch diameter in metres and N is speed in rpm.

figure.caption: The chain from duty to a checked design. Heat treatment sits between the material family and the hardness it must deliver, because the strength check uses hardness, not the steel grade.

spec.aria: A flow chart takes load and speed to a material family, then to heat treatment, then to surface hardness, then to a strength check.

examples.question: A 7.5 kW motor at 1440 rpm drives a 20-tooth pinion of module 3 mm with moderate shock. Find the pitch line velocity and the tangential load, and recommend a material pair.
steps: Pitch diameter: d = m z = 3 × 20 = 60 mm = 0.060 m.
Pitch line velocity: v = π d N / 60 = π × 0.060 × 1440 / 60 = 4.52 m/s.
Tangential load: Ft = 2T / d = 2 × 49.74 / 0.060 = 1658 N, about 1.66 kN.

Speed is below 5 m/s with moderate shock, so a through-hardened C45 pinion at about 250 BHN running with an FG 200 cast iron gear is a common shop-floor choice. Above 5 m/s, switch to a case-carburised 20MnCr5 pinion at 58–62 HRC with a hardened alloy gear 30–50 BHN softer.
examples.answer: Pitch line velocity is 4.52 m/s and tangential load is 1.66 kN; use a through-hardened C45 pinion at 250 BHN with a grey cast iron gear, moving to a case-carburised alloy pinion above 5 m/s.
examples.check:
import math
P = 7500.0
N = 1440.0
z = 20
m = 3.0
d = m * z / 1000.0
v = math.pi * d * N / 60.0
omega = 2.0 * math.pi * N / 60.0
T = P / omega
Ft = 2.0 * T / d
print(round(d * 1000.0, 1))
print(round(v, 2))
print(round(T, 2))
print(round(Ft, 1))

traps: Choosing the hardest steel for both wheels. The pinion needs the extra 30–50 BHN, and a hard case needs a tough core; a fully hardened tooth chips at the root.
Reading BHN as strength in MPa. 250 BHN is roughly 850 MPa tensile strength for steel as an estimate, but the allowable bending stress is a fraction of that.
Forgetting grinding stock. A carburised gear distorts; leave 0.1–0.2 mm per flank and specify 'grind after hardening'.
Pairing bronze with bronze in a worm drive, or a soft worm with a hard wheel. The wheel is the sacrificial member and the worm is hardened and ground.
Using cast iron for a high-speed pinion because it runs quietly. Damping does not repair low bending strength.

quiz.q: Define BHN and give its unit.
quiz.a: Brinell hardness number: hardness from a 10 mm steel ball pressed at 3000 kgf. Unit kgf/mm².

quiz.q: State the usual hardness difference between pinion and gear, and why it exists.
quiz.a: The pinion is 30–50 BHN harder, because it makes gear-ratio times more cycles; this balances the fatigue lives.

quiz.q: Why is a fully hard tooth worse than a case-hardened tooth under shock?
quiz.a: A fully hard tooth is brittle throughout, so the root cracks under shock. Case hardening gives a hard flank for wear and a tough core for bending.

quiz.q: Why is bronze used for the worm wheel and not the worm?
quiz.a: Worm contact is sliding, so the softer, embeddable, low-friction member is the wheel. The steel worm is hardened and ground and wears less.

quiz.q: A 3 kW, 960 rpm motor drives a 25-tooth pinion of module 2.5 mm. Find the pitch line velocity and state whether a through-hardened C45 pinion is acceptable.
quiz.a: d = 2.5 × 25 = 62.5 mm = 0.0625 m. v = π × 0.0625 × 960 / 60 = 3.14 m/s. Below 5 m/s, so C45 at about 250 BHN with a cast iron gear is acceptable.

quiz.q: A 300 BHN pinion meshes with a 300 BHN gear at 4:1 ratio. Predict the failure and give the fix.
quiz.a: The pinion makes four times the cycles at equal hardness, so it pits first. Raise the pinion to about 340 BHN, or reduce the ratio.

quiz.q: Why does nitriding suit an internal gear ring?
quiz.a: Nitriding needs no quench, so distortion is very small and internal teeth need no grinding, which is difficult to reach.

beyond: Not for the exam. Gear metallurgy is moving toward vacuum carburising and low-pressure carburising with gas quenching, which cut distortion and post-hardening grinding. Controlled shot peening of the root fillet raises bending fatigue life and is standard in automotive gearboxes. Powder-forged connecting rods and gears give near-net shape with good fatigue strength. Search for 'vacuum carburising', 'shot peening gear root' and 'powder metallurgy gears'.
